description: Single-panel AlN stability / solubility diagram for Fe–28Mn–10Al–0.8C low-density steel. The x-axis is [Al] in wt% (ticks 0–10 in steps of 2), the y-axis is [N] in wt% and is drawn with an axis break: the lower segment spans 0.00–0.02 and the upper segment 0.11–0.15 (ticks at 0.11, 0.12, 0.13, 0.14, 0.15), separated by zig-zag break marks. Three computed equilibrium curves divide the plot: a thin solid black line labelled "Smelting temperature (1873 K)", a blue dotted line labelled "Liquidus (1587 K)" and a red dashed line labelled "Solidus (1493 K)"; all three descend sharply at low [Al] then flatten to run almost horizontally at low [N] across the high-[Al] range, with the solidus line lying lowest. The field above the curves is labelled "AlN saturation" (upper-middle) and the field below them "No AlN" (lower-left). Two experimental alloy compositions are plotted as open symbols with printed coordinates: a grey circle for "HN steel" at (9.95, 0.1326) and a grey diamond for "LN steel" at (9.90, 0.0025). The figure demonstrates that the HN composition lies far above the equilibrium AlN line at the smelting temperature (AlN stable), whereas the LN composition lies below it (AlN not stable).

subfigures.description: AlN stability diagram, [Al] (wt%) vs [N] (wt%) with a broken y-axis (0.00-0.02 and 0.11-0.15). Three curves (solid black smelting temperature 1873 K, blue dotted liquidus 1587 K, red dashed solidus 1493 K) separate an 'AlN saturation' field above from a 'No AlN' field below. Two labelled data points: HN steel (grey circle) at (9.95, 0.1326) inside AlN saturation, and LN steel (grey diamond) at (9.90, 0.0025) in the No AlN field.

observations.observation: The plot is an AlN stability diagram with [Al] in wt% on the x-axis (0 to ~11, ticks every 2) and [N] in wt% on the y-axis, drawn with a broken axis (lower segment 0.00-0.02, upper segment 0.11-0.15).
Three equilibrium curves are plotted and named in the legend: 'Smelting temperature (1873 K)' (solid black line), 'Liquidus (1587 K)' (blue dotted line) and 'Solidus (1493 K)' (red dashed line).
The region above the equilibrium curves is labelled 'AlN saturation' and the region below them is labelled 'No AlN'.
The HN steel composition is plotted as an open grey circle at printed coordinates (9.95, 0.1326), located well inside the 'AlN saturation' field.
The LN steel composition is plotted as an open grey diamond at printed coordinates (9.90, 0.0025), located below the equilibrium curves in the 'No AlN' field.
The caption states the figure is the AlN stability diagram of Fe–28Mn–10Al–0.8C steels.
The citing text states the liquidus (1587 K) and solidus (1493 K) of the investigated steel were calculated using FactSage 8.0.
The citing text states that for LN steel the Al and N contents fell below the equilibrium line of the smelting temperature, suggesting AlN was not a stable phase during smelting.
The citing text states that for HN steel with 0.1326 wt% nitrogen the composition far exceeded the equilibrium line, so AlN inclusions can easily form and stably exist during smelting.
All three curves drop steeply below about 1 wt% Al and then run nearly horizontally at low [N] towards high [Al], the solidus lying lowest and the smelting-temperature line highest.
